name: connect-attached-follower
description: The default launch (a daemon plus an attached window) in a workspace where another window already runs the network: the daemon cannot own the relay, so the attached window opens the Connect screen read-only instead of printing /connect status text. It shows the network and this device, says in one plain line that another window runs the network, and offers no code, requests or accept/reject keys; /connect code says the same. Checked at 80 and 120 columns (issue #121, Story 1).

setup.description: throwaway HOME with one workspace on an offline network
setup.command: R=$(pwd); H="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/kollab-spec-connect-attached-follower"; rm -rf "$H"; mkdir -p "$H/.kollab" "$H/ws"; printf '%s' '{"kollabor":{"llm":{"active_profile":"openai-test","profiles":{"openai-test":{"provider":"openai","model":"gpt-5.5","base_url":"https://api.openai.com/v1","api_key":"sk-test-dummy","supports_tools":true}}}},"plugins":{"hub":{"enabled":true}}}' > "$H/.kollab/config.json"; ln -sfn "$R/plugins" "$H/ws/plugins"; cd "$H/ws" && HOME="$H" PYTHONPATH="$R" "$R/.venv/bin/python" -c "from plugins.hub.project_scope import resolve_project_root as root; from plugins.hub.relay_state import RelayStateStore as Store; s = Store(root(), None); s.state.origin = 'https://relay.invalid'; s.state.device_name = 'laptop-kollab'; s.save()"

setup.description: start a single-process window first (it owns the relay) and wait until it holds it
setup.command: R=$(pwd); H="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/kollab-spec-connect-attached-follower"; S=kollab-spec-attached-follower; tmux -L $S kill-server 2>/dev/null; tmux -L $S new-session -d -s owner -x 80 -y 30 && tmux -L $S send-keys -t owner -l "cd $H/ws && env HOME=$H KOLLAB_NO_KEYRING=1 PYTHONPATH=$R $R/.venv/bin/python $R/main.py --no-daemon" && tmux -L $S send-keys -t owner Enter; for i in $(seq 1 80); do [ $(find "$H/.kollab/network" -name relay-owner.json 2>/dev/null | wc -l) -ge 1 ] && break; sleep 0.5; done; [ $(find "$H/.kollab/network" -name relay-owner.json | wc -l) -ge 1 ]

steps.title: attached window whose daemon lost the relay: 80 columns

steps.pattern: another window in this workspace runs the network

steps.description: the screen is titled Connect, not printed as status text
it shows the workspace's network, read by the daemon
it shows this device

steps.pattern: ^ another window in this workspace runs the network; use /connect there *$
steps.description: one plain line says why nothing else is offered
the only key is esc
no code, requests, roster or decision keys that only the owner can carry out

steps.pattern: contact route|reconnect on launch disabled|\(this device\)
steps.description: not the /connect status text
no key or relay address
the title bar is exactly as wide as the terminal

steps.title: attached window: /connect code offers no code

steps.pattern: ^ another window in this workspace runs the network; use /connect there *$
steps.description: the code screen says the same one line
no code, and no key that would fail
widen this window to 120 columns (the runner is this shell's parent and names its tmux socket and session after its pid and this spec)
the screen is redrawn at 120 columns

steps.pattern: ^ another window in this workspace runs the network; use /connect there *$
steps.description: the plain line at 120
nothing to act on at 120 either

steps.title: the window that owns the relay keeps the full screen

steps.description: open /connect in the single-process window and read it
steps.command: S=kollab-spec-attached-follower; for c in / c o n n e c t; do tmux -L $S send-keys -t owner -l "$c"; sleep 0.06; done; tmux -L $S send-keys -t owner Enter; sleep 5; tmux -L $S capture-pane -t owner -p; tmux -L $S send-keys -t owner Escape

steps.description: the owner has the join code row
and the requests row
and its keys
the owner is not told another window owns the network

teardown.description: stop the daemon this launch forked (hub CLI of the throwaway HOME) and the single-process window
teardown.command: R=$(pwd); H="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/kollab-spec-connect-attached-follower"; cd "$H/ws" && HOME="$H" PYTHONPATH="$R" "$R/.venv/bin/python" "$R/main.py" --hub stop all; tmux -L kollab-spec-attached-follower kill-server
